title: Extending Use of Pro-family Leave to Provide Caregiving to Spouses
what_it_is: Extending Use of Pro-family Leave to Provide Caregiving to Spouses

sections.label: Pro-family leave for spouses
sections.summary: Asked whether teachers' pro-family leave could cover spouses, since it currently covers parents and children only; spouse care would be no-pay leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider including spouses in the category of people whom teachers are entitled to take pro-family leave to care for, as the current policy permits such leave to be taken to care for parents and children only.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: It is already part of the Civil Service provisions, as it stands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From what I understand, there are around 14 days of leave, but it has to be pre-qualified, of which I think, three days for childcare, two days for parent care, one day is for Housing and Development Board registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From what I understand, leave to take care of spouses would be considered no pay leave.
